title: Learnable Concept Catalog
description: Repo-independent, transferable engineering concepts. Deliberately separate from any knowledge base: a KB describes one system and is discarded when that system is, whereas the concept catalog accumulates across every repo you ever scan. This file is the durable artifact.

subject.description: `pattern` is a technique (idempotency, optimistic locking). `technology` is a product or service (EKS, Terraform remote state, GitHub Actions). Both use the same derivation, and that is the point: a technology explained from first principles transfers to its competitors, because what you learned was the trade-off rather than the product.

firstPrinciples.description: The derivation, not the definition. A definition tells you what a thing is called; this tells you why it had to exist, which is the part that transfers to systems you have not seen yet.

problem.description: The constraint in the world that forces the issue. No jargon allowed here.

naive.description: What you would obviously try first, and why it is reasonable.

failure.description: The specific scenario where the naive approach breaks. Concrete, not abstract.

resolution.description: The technique, derived as a response to that failure.

cost.description: What you gave up to get it. Every technique has one; a concept taught without its cost produces cargo-culting.

prerequisites.description: Concept ids that should be understood first. Forms the learning DAG.

probes.description: Active-recall prompts. Reading generates familiarity; answering generates knowledge.

kind.description: predict = asked BEFORE the code is revealed, so being wrong is the teaching moment. recall = retrieve a known fact. apply = transfer to a new situation. diagnose = spot what breaks.

detect.description: Rules that bind this concept to real code during a scan. This is what turns a static glossary into something anchored in your own repos.

kind.description: What to match against. Each maps to a field the extractors already populate.

note.description: Copied onto the binding to explain what the match means.
